existing_mechanism_inspected_first.candidate: the CORRECTED_SOURCE claim amendment (SOURCE_CORRECTED event) and register_source
reasons: it creates a new CLAIM version citing a DIFFERENT passage; the wrong time belongs to the SAME passage
the amendment event is stamped with the new availability, so an 'earlier' correction would appear in earlier as-of views as if it had been known then
it records no prior and corrected values, no evidence reference and no check against an out-of-date submission
register_source refuses a changed availability for an identical passage (the first registration stands)
a registered source can be cited by several claims; a claim-scoped amendment cannot correct it once

extension.size: one workspace-level event kind, SOURCE_AVAILABILITY_CORRECTED; one module v8/workbench/availability.py; one store method; one form and route
reused_controls: contract validation with every reason listed
refused form re-rendered with entries kept
extension.server_recorded_time: recorded_at, stamped by the server; the event carries NO source availability of its own
extension.no_migration: no workspace is migrated and no timestamp is fabricated; existing workspaces simply hold no such event

three_times.asserted_availability: as registered (never edited) and as corrected (the chain)

historical_view_semantics.statement: a view whose cutoff is at or after a correction's recorded time cuts every event citing the source by the corrected availability; a view at an earlier cutoff keeps the value the record held then and LISTS the correction as a later correction with what it would change
historical_view_semantics.why: a later correction is later knowledge: it must stay visible as later, must never make a source known earlier than the record held it, and must never revise a historical view silently
explained_in: the packaged operator guide and data dictionary

corrected_view: result (withdrawal counts as before the outcome only by availability)
eligibility_recomputed_beside_the_record.never_upgrades: a correction can make a record retrospective; it never makes a retrospective record contemporaneous

export_contract.events: the original SOURCE_REGISTERED event and the whole correction chain of every cited source
export_contract.block: `source_availability` (yuclaw-source-availability/1) and the row's `availability_corrections` exist ONLY when a correction exists
export_contract.earlier_exports: an export without a correction has the bytes it had before, so earlier exports verify under the schema they recorded (check reported as n/a, nothing reinterpreted)
export_contract.verifier: checks every link (registration, replaced value, recorded order, no availability of its own, contract fields) and re-derives the block from the packed events
export_contract.limit: exports are unsigned: a packet rebuilt wholesale with consistent content is a different export with a different canonical digest, as for every other block

cases: LATER: applies from its recorded time, only listed before it
EARLIER: never turns a later record into earlier knowledge; before the filing date refused
retry = one event; same op_id different content = conflict; out-of-date submission refused; two concurrent corrections record exactly one
corrected view beside the record with review codes; earlier adjudication retained; a further disputed adjudication may cite the correction
a correction never upgrades a retrospective record
export verified; seven altered counterparts refused (incl. matching hashes and digests); dataset export; fresh workspace over HTTP
an unrelated claim keeps its export identity
browser action under session/Origin/CSRF; entries kept; retry; stale refusal; as-of views

browser_demonstration.installed_cli: the corrected export verifies (rc 0) and the forged counterpart is refused (rc 1) through the installed command line, wheel and sdist
browser_demonstration.attribution: recorded by the automated journey runner as simulated test actions; not a human review

findings_while_verifying: the journey's first forged packet was refused by the chain check (stale `direction`) before the block comparison; the forgery was made self-consistent so that only recomputation can refuse it — the stronger case

limits: a corrected availability is an attributed assertion with an evidence reference, not a verified publisher clock
the scientific-link retrospective flag and the claim page's RETROSPECTIVE banner stay as recorded; the corrected view reports the difference
automated inspection and simulated actions only: no human or screen-reader review
